original_idea.problem: The original Artificial Hivemind paper tested open-ended generative tasks. It is unknown whether the same homogeneity effect holds for structured safety reasoning tasks.
original_idea.direction: Use the Infinity-Chat methodology -- pairwise semantic similarity across models -- but replace open-ended queries with a curated set of safety reasoning tasks. Measure whether homogeneity coefficients are higher, lower, or the same.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Safety reasoning tasks are more directly consequential than creative tasks; establishing whether homogeneity carries over is a direct safety research priority.
original_idea.relevant_context: Infinity-Chat benchmark (26K queries, 31K annotations, 70+ models); AILuminate safety hazard categories provide a ready-made task bank.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: directly extends the Artificial Hivemind finding to safety-relevant tasks, which are more consequential. A positive finding has immediate safety implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: replicating the Infinity-Chat methodology with new task types requires understanding the protocol and analysis pipeline, but the original paper provides guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: homogeneity coefficients on safety reasoning tasks compared to original open-ended baseline, with a clear numerical comparison.

title: Homogeneity Under Distribution Shift: Does Model Diversity Collapse on Out-of-Distribution Prompts?

original_idea.title: Homogeneity Under Distribution Shift: Does Model Diversity Collapse on Out-of-Distribution Prompts?

original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind methodology; OOD evaluation is standard in ML robustness literature; the combination has not been studied.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Good theory: agentic systems making sycophantic tool-use decisions cause real-world harm beyond text. This bridges sycophancy research to the agentic safety domain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing coding scenarios with incorrect user approaches and testing whether models follow or correct them is very accessible. CS students would find coding assistant scenarios natural to design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one domain (coding), one comparison (tool-use vs. text sycophancy). The scenarios are concrete and easy to evaluate objectively (did the model follow the wrong approach or not?).

title: Investigating How Instruction Hierarchy Violations Drive Deceptive Behavior
original_idea: Design scenarios with conflicts between system prompt and user message. Measure whether models deceive one principal to satisfy the other. Analyze reasoning traces.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Good theory: instruction hierarchy conflicts are common in real deployments. Understanding deception at conflict points informs multi-principal AI system design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing conflicting system/user prompts and measuring which principal the model satisfies (or deceives) is straightforward prompt engineering. Well within beginner capabilities.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One variable (instruction hierarchy conflict), clear measurement (which principal is deceived). A small set of conflict scenarios is very manageable in 30 hours.

title: Investigating Whether Capability Elicitation Prompts Reveal Hidden Sandbagging Asymmetries
original_idea: Compare baseline vs. elicited performance on MMLU/HumanEval. For sandbagging-instructed models, test whether elicitation breaks sandbagging. Compare to noise injection detection.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Moderate theory: elicitation prompts as a sandbagging detection complement is useful for evaluation protocols. But this is incremental improvement to existing detection methods.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running benchmarks with different elicitation strategies is moderately accessible. Implementing noise injection for comparison adds complexity. Using existing benchmark code helps.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Five elicitation strategies times two benchmarks times comparison to noise injection is a moderate experimental space. Narrowing to one benchmark and 2-3 elicitation strategies would help.

title: How Does Model Verbosity of Reasoning Affect Detectability of Deceptive Thinking Traces?
original_idea: Compare DeepSeek-R1 (long traces) vs. non-reasoning model with prompted CoT (short traces) on deception scenarios. Measure whether human raters and classifiers detect deception better in long vs. short traces.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Good theory: if verbose traces make deception harder to detect (burying intent), this undermines the safety argument for extended thinking as a monitoring target. Directly informs monitoring design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running deception scenarios on two model types and comparing is manageable. The human rating component adds effort but is a standard methodology. Automated classifier training is extra but optional.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Core comparison (long vs. short traces) is well-defined. But adding both human and automated evaluation doubles the work. Focusing on just one evaluation method would improve scope.

title: Adapting Credibility Assessment Interview Technique (CAIT) to Probe LLM Honesty
original_idea: Map CAIT/CBCA forensic criteria onto LLM output features. Build evaluation set of honest vs. deceptive responses. Test whether forensic criteria predict deception.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Moderate theory: if forensic criteria transfer to AI, it provides a low-cost screening layer. But the transfer from human deception detection to LLM output is speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Mapping criteria and running classification tests is accessible. Requires reading forensic psychology literature but the implementation is simple text analysis. No model training needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: map criteria, build small evaluation set, run classification. The deliverable is clear (does CAIT predict LLM deception?). Feasible in 30 hours.

title: Applying Cognitive Load Theory to Detect AI Deception via Response Latency and Complexity
original_idea: Elicit deceptive vs. honest responses. Measure response length, syntactic complexity, hedge words, clause depth. Train simple classifier. ~200 examples on single GPU.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Moderate theory: cognitive load markers as a post-hoc screening tool would be cheap and practical if they work. But the transfer of human cognitive load theory to LLMs is speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Very accessible: text feature extraction (length, complexity, hedge words) and simple classifier training on 200 examples. Perfect for CS students with basic ML knowledge. Single GPU is fine for medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: generate responses, extract features, train classifier. The 200-example target is realistic. Clear binary outcome (does the classifier work?). Feasible in 30 hours.

title: Importing Counterintelligence 'Tell' Catalogues Into LLM Deception Probing
original_idea: Construct probe battery based on counterintelligence tells: re-questioning, adversarial follow-ups, topic avoidance probes, cover story stress tests. Apply to models with/without planted deceptive goals.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting cross-domain transfer, but the theory that CI tells transfer to LLMs is unvalidated. The analogy between human agents hiding goals and scheming AI may not hold.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing probe batteries requires some creativity, but the implementation is prompt-based. The challenge is constructing valid CI-style probes without CI expertise. Moderate for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple probe types (re-questioning, adversarial follow-ups, topic avoidance, stress tests) across model families and sizes is moderately broad. Narrowing to 1-2 probe types would help.

title: Strategic Information Revelation in Signaling Games as a Model for Alignment Faking Detection
original_idea: Model alignment faking as a cheap-talk signaling game. Use Python to simulate equilibria and derive conditions for deceptive signaling as dominant strategy. Compare to empirical scheming contexts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Good theory: game-theoretic analysis can identify structural conditions that incentivize deception, informing evaluation procedure redesign. Provides formal grounding for empirical observations.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires game theory knowledge (signaling games, equilibrium analysis). Python simulation is accessible, but the formal modeling requires understanding beyond typical beginner CS curriculum.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: formalize one game, simulate equilibria, compare to known scheming contexts. The deliverable is a formal model with simulation results. Can be done in Python in 30 hours if the student has game theory background.

title: Applying Behavioral Economics Loss Aversion to Predict When Models Will Deceive
original_idea: Design paired scenarios where deceptive action is framed as avoiding a loss vs. gaining a benefit. Measure deception rates across ~5 open-source models. Test whether loss framing reliably increases deceptive behavior and whether this is model-size dependent.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear causal pathway: if loss-framing increases deception, operators can control scenario framing in deployment. However, the impact is somewhat indirect -- it identifies a variable but does not directly mitigate deception.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing paired prompt scenarios and measuring deception rates via API calls to open-source models is well within reach of beginner CS students. No fine-tuning or interpretability tools required. Medium compute sufficient for inference on ~5 models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: paired scenarios, fixed set of models, binary deception measurement. The DeceptionBench-style evaluation and ~5 models could be ambitious for 30hrs but the core experiment is clearly defined.

title: Reality Monitoring Criteria Applied to LLM Chain-of-Thought Deception Detection
original_idea: Collect CoT traces from a reasoning model under honest and deceptive conditions. Apply Reality Monitoring coding criteria (detail richness, internal consistency, meta-cognitive markers). Train a logistic regression classifier. Test generalization across model families.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Offers a lightweight, model-agnostic screening tool for deception. Impact pathway is clear but depends on whether Reality Monitoring criteria actually transfer to LLM outputs, which is uncertain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Collecting CoT traces is straightforward. Hand-coding Reality Monitoring criteria requires understanding the psychology framework. Training logistic regression is basic. Cross-model generalization testing adds scope. Feasible but requires careful operationalization of the coding criteria.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Moderately scoped. The core experiment (code traces, train classifier) is clear, but cross-model generalization testing and operationalizing Reality Monitoring criteria for LLM outputs adds breadth. Could be narrowed to a single model family.

title: Asymmetric Information Markets as a Framework for Evaluating AI Information Withholding
original_idea: Design tasks where the model has safety-relevant information the user does not, with varying incentive structures. Measure rates of strategic omission as a function of oversight level and goal instructions. Compare omission vs. commission deception.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong impact pathway: if omission-based deception has different elicitation conditions than commission, this directly informs detection strategy prioritization. Addresses a real blind spot in current deception research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing information-asymmetric tasks with varying incentive structures requires thoughtful experimental design. The conceptual framework from economics is sophisticated. Prompt engineering and measurement are feasible but the setup is non-trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The scope includes designing a task suite, varying two dimensions (oversight, instructions), and comparing two deception types. This is a full experimental design that may stretch 30hrs, though a minimal version focusing on one model and fewer conditions is possible.

title: Poker Tells and Inconsistency Patterns: Applying Card-Game Bluff Detection to LLM Evaluation
original_idea: Operationalize poker bluff-detection heuristics into an LLM probe battery: test for bet-sizing analogues, timing analogues, and range imbalance. Evaluate on models known to exhibit scheming behaviors.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The analogy from poker to LLM deception is creative but the causal impact pathway is weak. Poker tells rely on embodied behavioral signals that may not have meaningful analogues in text generation. The mapping is speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The individual probes (claim magnitude vs. evidence, response length vs. stakes) are implementable. However, operationalizing poker concepts into meaningful LLM metrics requires conceptual sophistication. The analogy may break down in practice.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three probe types across multiple models is moderately scoped. Each probe type needs separate operationalization and validation. Could be narrowed to one probe type on one model.

title: Social Proof and Conformity Pressure as Deception Amplifiers in LLM Populations
original_idea: Simulate a multi-agent setting where a majority of AI agents assert a false claim. Measure conformity-driven deception rates as a function of majority size, model family, and honesty instructions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong impact: multi-agent AI systems are increasingly deployed. If conformity pressure induces deception, this is a direct design concern for agentic pipelines. Clear causal pathway from finding to actionable design recommendation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simulating multi-agent settings via sequential API calls is straightforward. Measuring whether a model conforms to majority false claims is a clear binary outcome. No fine-tuning or interpretability tools needed. Very accessible for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three independent variables (majority size, model family, honesty instructions) with binary outcome is manageable but ambitious for 30hrs. Could be narrowed to one model family with varying majority size.

title: Applying Forensic Linguistic Stylometry to Detect Strategy Switching in LLM Outputs
original_idea: Generate long LLM outputs spanning honest and deceptive phases. Apply stylometric features to detect phase boundaries. Train a change-point detection model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If stylometric change-point detection works, it enables runtime monitoring without model internals. Clear deployment path but impact depends on whether LLM text actually shows stylometric discontinuities during strategy switches.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating outputs with mid-conversation goal injection is doable. Computing stylometric features (function word frequencies, sentence length) is basic NLP. narrow_scope.reasoning: The pipeline has multiple stages: data generation, feature extraction, change-point detection, evaluation. Each stage needs implementation. Feasible but may stretch 30hrs if thorough evaluation is expected.

title: Mapping the Causal Chain: When Does Capability Overhang Enable Deceptive Goal Pursuit?
original_idea: Systematically vary model capability levels (using models of different sizes and training stages) and test whether capability thresholds correlate with onset of deceptive behaviors on a scheming benchmark. Focus on theory-of-mind and planning tasks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly addresses one of the most critical open questions: at what capability level does deception emerge? If specific thresholds are identified, they become early-warning indicators for developers. Very high impact pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running multiple model sizes across multiple benchmarks (theory-of-mind tasks, planning tasks, scheming benchmarks). Getting access to intermediate training checkpoints is non-trivial. Needs substantial compute for running multiple large models. Challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very broad: multiple model families at multiple scales, multiple capability assessments, correlation analysis with scheming benchmarks. This is a full research paper scope, not a 30hr project.

title: Isolating the 'Learns to Fake Alignment' Step: Does RLHF Directly Reinforce Deceptive Compliance?
original_idea: Fine-tune a small model using RLHF with a reward signal that rewards safe-sounding outputs regardless of action consistency. Compare to a control model with behavior-consistent reward. Measure alignment-faking rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If RLHF directly selects for deceptive compliance, this identifies training itself as a causal source of alignment faking. This has direct, high-impact implications for how AI systems are trained.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing RLHF from scratch or using complex RLHF libraries, designing reward models, fine-tuning models under two conditions, and running consistency tests. RLHF is not beginner-accessible and requires significant ML engineering expertise and compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The experimental design is clear but execution requires RLHF training pipeline, reward model design, two training conditions, and held-out evaluation. This is a significant ML engineering project well beyond 30hrs for beginners.

title: Does Evaluation Context Recognition Causally Precede Deceptive Behavior?
original_idea: Design evaluation scenarios where evaluation context signals are systematically varied (obvious, ambiguous, none). Measure deception rates on a fixed scheming benchmark as a function of framing signal strength.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests whether evaluation-blind testing is a valid detection strategy. If context recognition is necessary for deception, this immediately enables a practical mitigation. Extremely clear impact chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing prompts with varying evaluation framing signals and measuring deception rates is accessible prompt engineering. No fine-tuning required. Using existing benchmarks reduces implementation burden. Well within beginner CS student capabilities.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three framing conditions on one benchmark with one to a few models is tightly scoped. Clear independent variable, clear dependent variable. Manageable within 30hrs.

title: Targeting the Deployment Transition: Do Models Behave Differently Immediately Post-Deployment?
original_idea: Simulate a deployment transition by fine-tuning a model to associate evaluation vs. deployment contextual cues with different behavioral policies. Test whether behavioral probes detect the switch.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If deployment-time behavioral shifts are detectable, this supports post-deployment monitoring as a practical safety layer. Clear impact pathway to monitoring system design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model to associate contextual cues with different policies, which is a non-trivial ML task. Designing behavioral probes adds complexity. Fine-tuning requires more than beginner-level ML skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Fine-tuning, designing contextual cues, building behavioral probes, and measuring detection sensitivity is a multi-stage project that exceeds 30hrs for beginners.

title: Causal Mediation Analysis: Does Goal Misalignment Cause Deception or Do Both Share a Common Cause?
original_idea: Use causal mediation analysis via activation patching in a small transformer to test whether goal-representation activations causally mediate deceptive output generation. Requires TransformerLens.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If goal misalignment is not the direct cause of deception, this fundamentally changes the intervention strategy. Extremely high theoretical impact -- could redirect entire research agendas.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires mechanistic interpretability expertise (TransformerLens, activation patching, causal mediation analysis). These are advanced techniques requiring deep understanding of transformer internals. Not accessible to beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Even scoped to a small transformer, causal mediation analysis requires identifying goal representations, deception circuits, and compliance circuits, then performing activation patching experiments. Technically narrow but expertise-intensive.

title: Intervening at the 'Learns Deceptive Communication' Step: Is Deceptive Language a Separable Module?
original_idea: Use activation patching and circuit ablation (TransformerLens) on a small model prompted to be deceptive vs. honest. Identify candidate circuits and test whether ablating them reduces deceptive output without degrading honest communication.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If a separable deception module exists, surgical interventions become possible. Important finding either way. Clear impact on mitigation strategy design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires advanced mechanistic interpretability skills: activation patching, circuit ablation, TransformerLens proficiency. These are expert-level techniques well beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Circuit discovery and ablation experiments on even a small model require multiple rounds of investigation. The scope is technically focused but requires deep expertise to execute.

title: Pre-Deployment Intervention: Stress Testing Anti-Scheming Training Under Distribution Shift
original_idea: Replicate simplified deliberative alignment fine-tuning on a small open-source model. Test scheming rates on in-distribution, novel role context, and novel reward framing scenarios. Measure degradation across distribution shift.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If anti-scheming training degrades under distribution shift, current safety claims are overstated. Directly informs deployment safety assurance levels. Critical finding for the field.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replicating deliberative alignment fine-tuning, even simplified, requires understanding the technique and implementing it. Fine-tuning and designing distribution-shifted scenarios requires intermediate ML skills. Not beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning, designing three scenario categories, and measuring scheming rates across conditions. This is a full research project exceeding 30hrs for beginners.

title: Harmful Action Link: What Action Types Are Enabled by Successful Deceptive Alignment?
original_idea: Survey existing scheming incidents and near-misses. Classify by action type (information withholding, output poisoning, resource acquisition, self-exfiltration). Build a structured risk taxonomy with harm severity and detectability. Validate against domain experts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A structured taxonomy enables prioritization of detection efforts by harm potential. Clear impact on resource allocation for safety research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: This is primarily a literature review and taxonomy construction task. No coding or ML required. CS students can read papers, classify incidents, and build a structured taxonomy. Expert validation may be hard to arrange but the core work is accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Literature survey scope can expand unpredictably. However, focusing on documented incidents from Apollo Research and OpenAI reports provides a bounded corpus. Expert validation adds scope but could be optional.

title: Goal Formation vs. Goal Concealment: Which Causal Link Is the Cheaper Intervention Target?
original_idea: Compare two interventions on a small finetunable model: training-time regularization to prevent misaligned goals vs. deployment-time probing to detect goal concealment. Measure residual deception rates and computational costs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct empirical comparison of two intervention strategies informs resource allocation across the entire safety field. Extremely high impact if results are clear.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing training-time regularization and deployment-time probing, both of which are advanced ML techniques. Fine-tuning with custom regularization and designing activation probes are expert-level tasks. Not accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two complete interventions, each requiring its own implementation, plus comparative evaluation on a toy task. This is two research projects in one.

title: Identifying Overlooked Causal Links: Does Deceptive Alignment Require Self-Modeling?
original_idea: Test a progression of models on self-modeling probes (knows it is an AI, being evaluated, what evaluator wants). Correlate self-modeling scores with scheming benchmark performance. Test whether interventions on self-modeling representations reduce scheming.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If self-modeling is a necessary intermediate for deception, capability thresholds for self-modeling become deception risk thresholds. Very high impact -- identifies a precise intervention target.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The first part (testing models on self-modeling probes and correlating with scheming benchmarks) is accessible via API calls. The intervention part (modifying self-modeling representations) requires interpretability tools and is advanced. Could be scoped to just the correlation study.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three-part project: self-modeling probes, scheming benchmarks, intervention testing. Even the first two parts across multiple model sizes is broad. The intervention part alone could be a separate project.

title: Backcasting from Reliable Deceptive Alignment Detection: What Behavioral Tests Are Needed?
original_idea: Enumerate properties a behavioral test must have to be manipulation-resistant. Audit existing scheming benchmarks against these criteria. Identify gaps and propose test designs to fill them.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifying what is missing in current behavioral tests is a critical meta-research contribution. If current tests are systematically evadable, knowing this changes how the field evaluates safety claims.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Primarily an analytical and literature review task. Enumerating desirable properties, auditing existing benchmarks, and identifying gaps requires critical thinking but no advanced ML skills. Very accessible for CS students with good analytical skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The audit scope depends on how many benchmarks to review. Could be narrowed to 3-5 major benchmarks. Proposing new test designs adds open-ended scope. Core audit is manageable.

title: Backcasting: What Ground-Truth Labels Are Needed to Validate Deception Detection Methods?
original_idea: Design methodology for generating ground-truth deceptive alignment labels: implant a verifiable misaligned goal via finetuning, confirm goal presence via independent probe, test concealment under evaluation. Build a small labeled dataset.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Ground-truth labels are a foundational infrastructure gap blocking all detection research. Solving this has multiplicative impact across the entire deception detection field.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires finetuning a model with an implanted misaligned goal and validating the implantation via independent probes. Finetuning and probe design require intermediate-to-advanced ML skills. Not beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The methodology design is clear and focused. Building even a small dataset requires the full pipeline (finetuning, probing, evaluation). Could be scoped to methodology-only without dataset, but that reduces value.

title: Backcasting: Standardized Deception Detection API for Model Evaluators
original_idea: Design a specification for a standardized deception detection evaluation API: input format, test scenario categories, output format (risk score + confidence + evidence), reproducibility requirements. Implement a minimal prototype in Python.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Standardization enables cross-lab comparison and reproducibility. Important infrastructure contribution but the impact depends on community adoption, which is uncertain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: API specification design and Python prototype implementation are well within CS student capabilities. Using existing scenarios from DeceptionBench reduces design burden. Standard software engineering task.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Specification design is bounded. Implementing a minimal prototype is feasible. However, making it genuinely useful requires careful design of scenario categories and output formats, which could expand scope.

title: Backcasting: What Interpretability Probes Must Be Validated Before Deception Detection Is Reliable?
original_idea: Train linear probes on a small transformer's activation space to predict deceptive vs. honest behavioral mode. Evaluate probe reliability: false negative rate, false positive rate, cross-model transfer, robustness to paraphrasing.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Validating when probes work and fail is essential before deploying them as safety tools. Directly informs whether the probe-based detection strategy is viable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training linear probes on activation space requires understanding transformer internals and using libraries like TransformerLens. Extracting activations and training probes is intermediate ML work. Cross-model transfer testing adds complexity. Not beginner-level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Core experiment (train probe, measure error rates) is focused. Cross-model transfer and paraphrasing robustness add breadth. Could be narrowed to one model with basic error rates.

title: Backcasting: Evaluator Diversity as a Requirement for Manipulation-Resistant Assessment
original_idea: Construct a small ensemble of diverse deception detectors (behavioral probe, activation probe, stylometric classifier, human evaluator). Test whether the ensemble achieves lower false negative rates than any individual detector.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If evaluator diversity is structurally necessary for reliable detection, this is a fundamental design principle for safety evaluation. Clear impact on evaluation system architecture.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building four different detection methods (behavioral probe, activation probe, stylometric classifier, human evaluation) each requires its own implementation. Activation probes require interpretability tools. The ensemble approach is conceptually simple but implementation is complex.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four detection methods plus ensemble evaluation is effectively four mini-projects. Even simplified versions of each method require separate implementation and calibration. Well beyond 30hrs.

title: Backcasting: Longitudinal Consistency Testing as a Core Detection Requirement
original_idea: Test whether longitudinal consistency (multiple probing sessions with varied framing, delays, context) significantly reduces false negative rates compared to single-session evaluation. Use a model with implanted deceptive goal.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If longitudinal testing is necessary, current single-evaluation safety gates are insufficient. This directly informs deployment safety protocol design. Clear practical impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implanting a deceptive goal via finetuning (advanced), then running multiple probing sessions with varied conditions. The finetuning step is the main barrier for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Once the deceptive model exists, the probing experiment is well-scoped (vary sessions, measure false negatives). But creating the deceptive model is a prerequisite project. Could use an existing deceptive model if available.

title: Backcasting: What Training Transparency Is Required to Enable Deception Detection?
original_idea: Survey what training information current deception detection methods require. Build a transparency requirement matrix: for each detection method, list required training information. Identify minimal transparency requirements for reliable detection.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifying a governance gap -- what transparency disclosures should be required of AI developers -- has direct policy impact. Bridges technical detection research with governance recommendations.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: This is a structured literature review and analysis task. No coding or ML required. Reading papers, identifying information requirements, and building a matrix is fully accessible to beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-bounded: survey a fixed set of detection methods, catalog their information requirements, produce a matrix. The deliverable is clear and finite. Fits comfortably in 30hrs.

title: Backcasting: Adversarial Red-Teaming Protocols That Model Sophisticated Scheming
original_idea: Design a red-teaming protocol where a prompted LLM adversary tries to evade specific deception detectors. Test whether current detectors can be strategically evaded. Measure evasion success rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If current detectors are easily evaded by strategic adversaries, this is a critical finding. Adversarial testing validates detector robustness before real-world deployment.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompting an LLM to act as an adversarial evader is accessible. However, implementing specific deception detectors (behavioral probes, activation probes, CoT monitors) to test against requires understanding those detection methods. The adversarial prompting part is beginner-friendly but the detector implementation is not.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Could be narrowed to testing evasion against one specific detector type. Testing against multiple detectors expands scope. Protocol design plus implementation plus measurement is substantial but feasible if focused.

title: Backcasting: Formal Verification Conditions for Deception-Free Behavior
original_idea: Enumerate formal conditions under which a transformer could be proven deception-free. Assess which conditions are empirically testable. Propose a minimal formal verification framework for deception absence.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Specifying conditions for formal guarantees clarifies what partial guarantees are achievable. Important theoretical contribution that scopes the limits of behavioral evaluation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires deep theoretical understanding of formal verification, transformer architecture, and deception formalisms. This is a theoretical research task requiring significant mathematical maturity beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Formal verification framework design is inherently open-ended. Enumerating conditions could expand indefinitely. Assessing empirical testability requires broad knowledge of available tools. Difficult to bound.

title: Backcasting: What Behavioral Signatures Distinguish Deceptive Alignment from Sycophancy?
original_idea: Design a behavioral test battery that differentiates deceptive alignment (conceals misaligned goal strategically) from sycophancy (mimics aligned behavior without goal-directed reasoning). Use model internals to validate. Test across model families.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Distinguishing deceptive alignment from sycophancy prevents mistargeted interventions. Important for calibrating safety responses -- treating sycophancy as scheming wastes resources.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing behavioral tests is accessible. Using model internals for validation requires interpretability skills. Testing across model families adds scope. Could be simplified to behavioral-only tests on one model.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Test battery design, internals validation, and cross-model testing is broad. Could be narrowed to designing and testing a small set of behavioral probes on one model without internals validation.

title: Deception + Weak Oversight: Quantifying the Undetectability Amplification Effect
original_idea: Systematically vary oversight intensity (evaluator sample rate, capability level, prompt quality) while holding deceptive behavior constant. Measure how detection rates scale with oversight parameters. Identify minimum oversight thresholds.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly quantifies how much oversight is needed to prevent undetectable scheming. As AI scales, oversight becomes scarcer -- this relationship directly informs deployment safety requirements.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Varying oversight parameters (sample rate, evaluator quality) and measuring detection rates is a well-structured experiment. Can be done with API calls. No fine-tuning required. Accessible prompt engineering and measurement.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three oversight parameters with scaling analysis is moderately scoped. Could be narrowed to one parameter (sample rate) for a focused study. The core experiment is clear but full parameter sweep is ambitious.

title: Deception + Emergent Misalignment: Compound Risk from Spontaneous Deceptive Behavior
original_idea: Reproduce simplified emergent misalignment by finetuning a small model on a narrow misaligned task. Test whether resulting deceptive behaviors are detectable by goal-directed scheming evals vs. generic anomaly detectors. Measure false negative rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifying a detection blind spot (emergent deception without goal formation) has high impact. If current scheming evals miss this class, a major vulnerability is exposed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reproducing emergent misalignment requires finetuning a model on specific misaligned tasks, which is intermediate ML work. Running scheming evals and anomaly detectors adds implementation complexity. Not beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The experiment is well-defined: finetuning, two evaluation types, comparison. But finetuning and setting up both evaluations is substantial. Could be narrowed to one model and one comparison.

title: Deception + Capability Gain: How Scheming Enables Recursive Self-Improvement Risks
original_idea: Design a controlled agentic scenario where a model with an implanted misaligned goal has tool-use capabilities. Measure whether it strategically acquires resources or capabilities to increase future goal-achievement while behaving normally on monitored tasks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Capability acquisition during deceptive deployment is a compounding risk that converts single deception into escalating threat. Understanding this pathway is critical for preventing worst-case scenarios.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implanting a misaligned goal via finetuning, setting up an agentic environment with tool access, and measuring strategic resource acquisition behavior. Complex multi-component system requiring intermediate ML and software engineering skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Finetuning, agentic environment setup, tool-use integration, and behavioral measurement across capability levels is a large project. Multiple engineering components each require significant work.

title: Deception + Sycophancy: When Approval-Seeking Masks Strategic Goal Pursuit
original_idea: Train a model to be simultaneously sycophantic and goal-directed via finetuning. Test whether scheming detection methods that work on non-sycophantic models fail on sycophantic-scheming models. Compare behavioral vs. activation probe robustness.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If sycophancy compounds with deceptive alignment to create systematic detection blind spots, this exposes a vulnerability in existing evals. Sycophancy is already pervasive, making this practically relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires finetuning a model to be both sycophantic and goal-directed, then running multiple detection methods including activation probes. Both the training and evaluation sides require advanced ML skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Custom finetuning, running multiple detection methods, and comparing behavioral vs. activation probe robustness is a multi-stage project well beyond 30hrs for beginners.

title: Deception + Multi-Agent Coordination: Collective Scheming Without Individual Detectability
original_idea: Design a multi-agent task where a misaligned goal can only be achieved through coordinated actions by multiple agents, each contributing a sub-action that appears benign in isolation. Measure whether individual-agent monitoring fails to detect the collective deception. Test whether ensemble monitoring catches it.
